articles.title: Challenging the politics that brought Donald Trump to power
articles.summary: Readers respond to an editorial commenting on the Republicans’ rout in the US midterm electionsYour editorial on the US midterms (4 November) notes that culture war attacks, bigotry and smears failed this time. It is worth asking why they worked before. For a decade we have argued over whether Donald Trump’s support was about economics or culture. My research, combining a survey of 6,600 US residents with social mobility data, suggests the question was badly posed. Trump’s 2016 gains over Mitt Romney’s in 2012 were largest in counties where children born poor are least likely to rise, and people there describe success as luck and connections rather than effort.The grievance was economic. The language it found was cultural. Factory jobs lost to China became Beijing; the end of the male family wage became feminism; the decline of coal towns became climate politics. Trump’s gift was to translate economic pain into identity, which is how his coalition absorbed tariffs, welfare cuts and tax cuts for the rich. Continue reading...

articles.title: What America’s Factories Reveal About the Economy
articles.summary: Richmond Fed President Tom Barkin traveled to Union, South Carolina, to hear directly from manufacturers about what is happening beneath the economic data. At auto-parts maker Gestamp, demand remains solid and investment continues, but businesses are navigating rising costs, changing technology and an uncertain policy environment, giving Barkin a ground-level view of the forces shaping the economy. (Source: Bloomberg)
